node.rich_text:
## What is `package.json`?
It's the **identity card and instruction manual** for your frontend project. Every Node.js/Next.js project must have one.
---
### Breaking down YOUR `package.json`:
#### Project info ```json "name": "frontend", "version": "0.1.0", "private": true ← can't be accidentally published to npm ```
---
#### Scripts — commands you can run ```json "scripts": { "dev": "next dev", ← npm run dev → starts dev server (localhost:3000) "build": "next build", ← npm run build → builds for production "start": "next start", ← npm run start → runs production build "lint": "eslint" ← npm run lint → checks code for errors } ```
These are the 4 commands you use daily: ```bash npm run dev # development — you use this npm run build # production build npm run start # run production build npm run lint # check for code errors ```
---
#### Dependencies — needed to RUN the app ```json "dependencies": { "next": "16.2.3", ← Next.js framework "react": "19.2.4", ← React library "react-dom": "19.2.4" ← React DOM rendering } ``` Only 3 runtime dependencies — very minimal and clean.
---
#### DevDependencies — needed only during DEVELOPMENT ```json "devDependencies": { "@tailwindcss/postcss": "^4", ← Tailwind CSS processor "@types/node": "^20", ← TypeScript types for Node.js "@types/react": "^19", ← TypeScript types for React "@types/react-dom": "^19", ← TypeScript types for React DOM "eslint": "^9", ← code linter "eslint-config-next": "16.2.3",← Next.js ESLint rules "tailwindcss": "^4", ← CSS utility framework "typescript": "^5" ← TypeScript compiler } ``` These are NOT included in the final production build — only used while coding.
---
#### allowScripts — security whitelist ```json "allowScripts": { "sharp@0.34.5": true, ← image optimization library "unrs-resolver@1.11.1": true ← module resolver } ``` Explicitly allows these packages to run install scripts — a security feature.
---
### Summary:
``` package.json = project ID card + command list + dependency list
Most important parts: scripts → commands you run (dev, build, lint) dependencies → what the app needs to work devDependencies → what YOU need to develop it ```
